title: INDECOPI software accreditation (Guide v4.0)
description: The automated part of an INDECOPI (IOFE, Peru) accreditation of signing and verification software (Guía de Acreditación de Software v4.0, annex B): each step runs against the Sandbox with the IOFE policy, through the library and the CLI, cross-validated with EU DSS when one is connected. Tags name the items of annex B of the guide (F-n: section 4.2, signing by an automated agent; V-n: section 4.3, verification by automated agents; S-n: section 4.4, time-stamps) and a topic; docs/playbooks/indecopi-checklist.md maps every item to a step, a test or what is left to the accredited product. It complements sandbox-basics and etsi-baseline: the checks any signer or validator makes whatever the policy (revocation, validity, time-stamps, levels, algorithms, changed files) are shown there, and the checklist names those steps; here are only the ones the IOFE profile and policies decide (the TSL, nonRepudiation for an automated agent), the report and the audit trail.

sections.title: Trusted list (TSL)
sections.description: The iofe profile on the Sandbox: the trust anchors come from the Sandbox's trusted list (/tl/tl.xml), read as IofeExtension reads INDECOPI's (IofeExtension.DefaultListOptions: the CA services and the services typed 'unspecified', as INDECOPI types its TSAs and signature software, never a code-signing certificate); its signature is checked against the operator's certificate.

steps.title: Sign with a root listed in the TSL
steps.description: The Sandbox's TSL is downloaded, its signature is checked with the operator's certificate, and the signer's root is listed: the signature is made.

steps.title: TSL signed by another key: refused
steps.description: The Sandbox publishes a TSL signed by a key that is not the operator's (a fake TSL): there are no anchors and the signature is refused.

steps.title: Tampered TSL: refused
steps.description: The Sandbox publishes a TSL whose content changed after it was signed, so its XML signature breaks: it must not be used, there are no anchors, and signing is refused (UntrustedRoot).

steps.title: Expired TSL: refused
steps.description: The published TSL has its NextUpdate in the past.

steps.title: Time-stamp from a TSA whose CA the TSL lists as 'unspecified'
steps.description: As INDECOPI lists the Llama.pe Timestamping CA (not its TSU) with the service type 'unspecified', the TSL names the self-signed CA of the Sandbox's IOFE TSA: its time-stamp chains to that service and the signature is made. Not cross-validated: DSS trusts every granted service of the list whatever its type, so it does not show the 'unspecified' rule this step is about.

steps.title: Same TSA without the TSL: refused
steps.description: With the Sandbox root as the only anchor, the IOFE TSA chains to nothing trusted: the 'unspecified' service of the TSL is what makes it trusted in tsl-tsa-unspecified.

steps.title: Validate with anchors from the TSL
steps.description: Validates the tsl-ok file with the anchors read from the TSL and the IOFE validation policy: valid.

steps.title: Validate with a fake TSL
steps.description: Validates the same file while the TSL is signed by another key: the fake list gives no anchors, so NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND.

steps.title: Validate with an expired TSL
steps.description: Validates it while the TSL is past its NextUpdate: the IOFE policy's TLNotExpired fails, so the validator asks to try later (INDETERMINATE / TRY_LATER) instead of accepting.

steps.title: Validate a time-stamp whose TSA's CA the TSL lists as 'unspecified'
steps.description: Validates the B-T file whose TSA chains to a CA the TSL lists as 'unspecified': the time-stamp is trusted through the list, so the signature is valid.

sections.title: Key usage of an automated agent
sections.description: Section 4.2 asks an automated agent to check the nonRepudiation bit, and section 4.3 the software verifying what agents receive: the iofe policies with KeyUsage = nonRepudiation (declared in policies). The other certificate checks (validity, a key usage not meant for signing, revocation) are the same under any policy: sandbox-basics shows them.

steps.title: Sign with a certificate without nonRepudiation (to validate)
steps.description: The iofe signing policy accepts digitalSignature or nonRepudiation (as section 4.1 does for end-user software); the file is used by the validation step that requires nonRepudiation.

steps.title: Automated agent: a certificate without nonRepudiation is refused
steps.description: Section 4.2 (annex B item 12) asks an automated agent to check the nonRepudiation bit: the iofe policy with KeyUsage = nonRepudiation (playbook:iofe-agent) refuses a certificate that has digitalSignature only.

steps.title: Signer with neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation (minimal signing policy, to validate)
steps.description: Signs with a certificate whose key usage allows neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation, under the minimal signing policy and without validating, only to produce the file v-key-usage validates.

steps.title: IOFE validation: a signer with neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation is not accepted
steps.description: The IOFE validation policy requires digitalSignature or nonRepudiation in the signing certificate (Req. 23), where the library's default only warns: the certificate without either fails the constraint (INDETERMINATE).

steps.title: Validation requires nonRepudiation: not accepted
steps.description: With the iofe policy requiring nonRepudiation (playbook:iofe-agent-validation) the certificate without it fails the chain constraint (EN 319 102-1: INDETERMINATE).

sections.title: Validation report
sections.description: What the guide asks a viewer to show the signer and the relying parties (F-30, V-30), in Spanish.

steps.title: Validation report of a signature trusted through the TSL
steps.description: Validates the tsl-ok file as INDECOPI's relying parties would (anchors from the TSL, IOFE policy): the report shows integrity, signing time, public key and certificate data; the CLI writes it as HTML with simplesign validate --html-report report.html --report-language es.

sections.title: Audit log
sections.description: The audit trail the guide asks of signing software (F-15, V-15): every attempt, made or refused, leaves a record.

steps.title: Audit record of each signature
steps.description: Each signature made or refused is recorded (certificate, policy, input and output hashes, reason) in a hash-chained log; the CLI checks it with simplesign audit verify.

steps.title: A refused signature is recorded too
steps.description: A refused signature (a revoked certificate) with the audit log on: the attempt must be recorded too, with its refusal, not only the signatures made.
